items.title: Nanta: Pan Borneo highway contracts cannot be terminated arbitrarily
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Contracts of companies involved in the construction of the Pan Borneo Highway cannot be terminated arbitrarily, as delays in individual work packages are not necessarily caused solely by the contractors' shortcomings. Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said that when contractors applied for an extension of time (EOT), the Works Ministry (KKR) had to assess whether the delays were caused by constraints on the part of government agencies or other factors. He said only one contractor had so far had its contract terminated over delays in the project, following a comprehensive assessment.

items.title: Schools evacuated across Italy after bomb threats
items.summary: ROME: Schools were evacuated across Italy on Wednesday following a series of hoax bomb threats, but Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said there was no "concrete danger." Meloni said she had called a government meeting later on Wednesday after 312 schools received threats, according to Italian media.--AFP MORE TO COME © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Nanta confirms he will remain Kapit MP, not contest Sarawak polls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Kapit Member of Parliament Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi has confirmed that he will continue serving at parliamentary level and will not contest a State Legislative Assembly (DUN) seat in next month’s Sarawak election. The Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) secretary-general said speculation about him contesting at state level arose after a proposal to create a new constituency, DUN Melekun, under the Kapit parliamentary constituency. On July 7, 2025, the Sarawak DUN passed the State Legislative Assembly (Composition of Membership) Bill 2025, approving 17 additional seats and bringing the total number of state seats to 99.

items.title: RM488mil modular data centre in Senai expected to be completed in Q1 2027
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU: EPG's Malaysian Free Industrial Zone (FIZ) factory EPG Modular Data Center worth RM488 million in Senai Airport City (SAC) is expected to be completed in the first quarter of 2027. The factory, located in an integrated industrial development area of approximately 1,100 hectares in Iskandar Malaysia, covers an area of 107,450 square metres, including 70,000 square metres of production space. Meanwhile, Senai Airport City chief executive officer Gan Seng Keong said EPG's investment is a significant addition to the growing data centre manufacturing ecosystem at SAC.

items.title: IGP says Prisons Dept responsible for Najib’s home security
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — The Prisons Department is fully responsible for the security arrangements for former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak, who has been serving the remainder of his jail sentence under house arrest at his residence in Langgak Duta here since yesterday. Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), as a law enforcement agency, maintained close cooperation with the Prisons Department to ensure compliance with the security requirements. Mohd Khalid said PDRM had assigned several officers to assist the Prisons Department throughout the former prime minister’s period of serving the remainder of his sentence at home.

items.title: Selangor plans country's first wakaf hospital
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Perbadanan Wakaf Selangor is planning to develop the country's first wakaf hospital to address a shortage of hospital beds and treatment facilities. "It is our aspiration to develop a wakaf hospital. Perbadanan Wakaf Selangor also plans to develop other wakaf assets, including wakaf elderly care homes, as Selangor moves towards becoming an ageing state.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM NOV 11, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia's 30-stock index closed lower as stronger-than-expected US inflation reinforced expectations of a higher-for-longer Federal Reserve policy stance, prompting investors to reassess global risk exposure. The key index dropped more than 8 points to 1,595. In the crypto exchange, Bitcoin dropped to RM301,821.

items.title: Melaka polls: Investments to create jobs for Melaka people, says Ab Rauf
items.summary: MASJID TANAH: Investments coming into Melaka are expected to generate employment opportunities for the people, particularly as companies need workers to operate their businesses, said Melaka Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh. "Investments certainly reflect the job opportunities available and the workforce that the state government will provide. "This will also create employment opportunities for the people," he said after visiting the Ayer Limau state constituency operations room today.

items.title: Ringgit ends mostly higher against major and regional currencies
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit ended mostly higher on Wednesday against major and regional currencies but eased against the greenback amid renewed expectations of a hike in US interest rates. This comes following stronger-than-expected US inflation data. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the ringgit fell by almost 0.45 per cent against the greenback today as stronger-than-expected US inflation fuelled expectations of a rate hike in December.

items.title: Melaka polls: Packed schedule does not stop Rais from visiting flood victims
items.summary: MELAKA: Even with his campaign schedule in Sungai Udang running at full pace, Barisan Nasional candidate Datuk Rais Yasin took time to visit families affected by floods in Kampung Gapam, Bemban, Jasin, last night. The floods affected seven houses, prompting Rais, who previously served as the state's senior executive councillor for housing, local government, drainage, climate change and disaster management, to visit the area. The people's problems must take priority.

items.title: MMAG Holdings' bank accounts freed from AMLA restrictions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: MMAG Holdings Bhd said restrictions imposed on certain bank accounts belonging to the company and its subsidiaries under the Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA) have been lifted. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, the company said the affected accounts are no longer subject to restrictions previously imposed by the Royal Malaysia Police's (PDRM) Anti-Money Laundering Investigation Team. MMAG shares closed one sen, or 33.33 per cent, higher at four sen today.

items.title: Government steps in with RM15m monthly subsidy as palm oil costs rise
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — The government has approved a special incentive of about RM15 million a month under the Cooking Oil Price Control Mechanism (MKHMM) to maintain ceiling prices and ensure a stable supply of bottled pure palm cooking oil. Armizan said the sustained increase in global CPO prices since June 2025 had placed mounting cost pressures on manufacturers, prompting some companies to halt production of bottled cooking oil. Meanwhile, PRESMA president Datuk Mohammed Mosin Abdul Razak said stable cooking oil prices would help restaurant operators better manage their business costs.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Wednesday, Nov 11, 2026
items.summary: MISSED what happened today? Here's a glimpse at what happened throughout the country in photographs. [[nid:1575583]] [[nid:1575582]] [[nid:1575581]] [[nid:1575580]] [[nid:1575579]] © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Car washer charged with murder over fatal crash on Jalan Kuching
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A car washer was brought before the Magistrate's Court today on a charge of murdering a lorry driver in a fatal accident on Jalan Kuching here earlier this month. He is accused of killing Indonesian lorry driver Yudi Hartono, 39, on Jalan Kuching heading from the city centre towards Segambut at 4.44 am on Nov 4. Meanwhile, in a statement today, Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief ACP Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said that preliminary investigations found the car driven by the accused, with a 46-year-old male passenger, had struck the rear right side of the lorry.

items.title: JAC rolls out first locally assembled PHEV pickup
items.summary: EVOLVELECTRIC Motors Sdn Bhd has launched the JAC T9 plug-in hybrid electric vehicle (PHEV) petrol, introducing what it says is Malaysia's first locally assembled plug-in hybrid pickup truck. The JAC T9 PHEV Petrol is currently the only plug-in hybrid pickup available in the Malaysian market, combining a conventional 4x4 setup with electric propulsion and extended driving range. Power comes from a 2.0-litre turbocharged petrol engine paired with an electric four-wheel-drive dual-motor system and a 4DHT hybrid transmission.

items.title: Car washer charged with murder over fatal Jalan Kuching crash that killed lorry driver
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — A car washer was brought before the Magistrate’s Court today on a charge of murdering a lorry driver in a fatal accident on Jalan Kuching here earlier this month. He is accused of killing Indonesian lorry driver Yudi Hartono, 39, on Jalan Kuching heading from the city centre towards Segambut at 4.44am on November 4. Meanwhile, in a statement today, Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief ACP Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said that preliminary investigations found the car driven by the accused, with a 46-year-old male passenger, had struck the rear right side of the lorry.

items.title: Betamek's Q2 net profits fell 32pct; declares 1.25 sen dividend per share
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR:Betamek Bhd's net profit fell 32.1 per cent in the second quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, at RM7.1 million, from RM10.4 million a year ago, due to higher operating expenses and lower margins. Revenue for the quarter increased by RM9.02 million or 12.44 per cent to RM81.49 million, mainly due to higher export sales, which increased by RM9.99 million, partially offset by slightly lower local sales, Betamek said. Connectivity modules contributed RM7.12 million, while non-automotive products accounted for RM7.88 million.

items.title: Oppstar recorded narrower net loss in Q2 as revenue surges 71pct
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Oppstar Bhd registered narrower net loss of RM62,000 in the second quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q2 FY27), compared with RM3.2 million a year ago, as revenue surged 71 per cent to RM12.6 million. The higher revenue translated into RM7,000 profit before tax during the quarter, a sharp turn from a loss before tax of RM3.32 million in the same quarter last year, the integrated circuit (IC) design company said. Revenue from specific design services grew by RM3.79 million due to heightened demand for engineering services, while post-silicon validation services saw a RM1.45 million increase driven by customer demand, said Oppstar.

items.title: Azalina: Land acquisition must uphold rule of law, respect constitutional safeguards
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Challenging decisions involving compulsory land acquisition is not an act of disloyalty but an essential part of upholding the rule of law, said Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. The Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) said that as Malaysia continued to pursue economic growth and modernise its infrastructure, compulsory land acquisition remained a necessary but sensitive public duty requiring transparency, procedural fairness and adequate compensation. “From the perspective of democracy, challenging the exercise of power is not an act of disloyalty, rather it’s an essential part of the rule of law,” she said at the “Challenging Land Acquisition in Malaysia” book launch here today.

items.title: Foreign driver arrested after driving against traffic in Kempas
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: A foreign driver was arrested after driving against traffic and sideswiping a Honda Civic in Kempas. The 32-year-old was driving a Toyota Harrier along Jalan Banjaran Utama yesterday when he entered the opposing lane and collided with a Honda Civic driven by a 26-year-old Malaysian. Johor Baru (North) police chief Assistant Commissioner Azrol Anuar Nor said the impact caused the Harrier to veer off to the left side of the road.

items.title: Pejuang proposes phased closure of UNHCR office in Malaysia
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Parti Pejuang Tanahair (Pejuang) has submitted memorandums to the Home and Foreign Ministries calling for a comprehensive review of refugee management in Malaysia, including the possibility of gradually closing the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) office in the country. When contacted, Pejuang information chief Muhammad Rafique Rashid Ali called on the government to consider gradually transferring refugee registration, identification, monitoring and case management responsibilities to Malaysian authorities. The memorandum outlined 10 key demands, including an independent audit of existing refugee management mechanisms and the establishment of a comprehensive government-controlled refugee database.

items.title: IGP: 35 Police personnel recognised for rejecting and reporting corruption this year
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 35 police officers and personnel have been recognised this year for their firmness and courage in rejecting and reporting acts of corruption, said Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail. He said that of the total, six received the Inspector-General of Police's Letter of Appreciation, 13 received Certificates of Appreciation and Financial Rewards from the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) and 16 received MACC Certificates of Appreciation. He said that based on MACC statistics, the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) was among the government agencies with the highest number of recipients of such recognition, involving 437 officers and personnel between 2012 and 2025.

items.title: War cost Gulf over US$200bil in damage, US$790bil losses until 2030
items.summary: DUBAI: The US-Iran war will cost Gulf countries more than US$200 billion in damage and economic losses could reach nearly four times that amount by 2030, insurer Allianz Trade said on Wednesday. Gulf countries bore the brunt of Teheran's wrath after the United States and Israel launched attacks on Iran on Feb 28, triggering the war. "Physical damage across the region is assessed just above US$200bn, mostly concentrated in Hormuz-locked economies, especially in energy infrastructure," the insurer said in a report.

items.title: Zahid tells Mat Sabu to surrender ministerial allowances too [WATCH]
items.summary: AYER KEROH: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has backed Mohamad Sabu's decision to forfeit his entire ministerial salary to support groups campaigning for equal house arrest rights for prisoners. Zahid said the Amanah president should also give up his ministerial allowances if he genuinely wanted to support the cause. "A minister's basic salary is modest, but the allowances are substantial — he shouldn't keep the allowances," he added.

items.title: Sri Lanka launches pilot of Chinese flying taxi service
items.summary: COLOMBO: Sri Lanka has authorised a Chinese manufacturer to begin testing a pilotless two-seater air taxi, authorities announced Wednesday at a flight demonstration in Colombo. The Civil Aviation Authority said a licence had been granted to EHang to test its two-seater, pilotless electric aircraft with vertical take-off and landing capability. Kodithuwakku said Sri Lanka was also joining a race among more than a dozen countries to introduce passenger-drone services.

items.title: United Plantations reports 43pct higher net profits in Q3; warns of workers shortages
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: United Plantations Bhd's net profit rose 43.1 per cent to RM290.93 million in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 from RM203.28 million a year ago, on the back of higher production volume. Revenue for the quarter under review climbed 6.7 per cent year-on-year to RM722.22 million from RM677.08 million last year, while profit before tax jumped 34.8 per cent to RM380.9 million. For the nine-month period, the company's earnings increased 4.8 per cent to RM645.58 million from RM615.92 million a year ago, on the back of 9.4 per cent higher revenue at RM2 billion.

items.title: 4 injured as factory van hits broken-down bus on Johor highway
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Four workers heading to Singapore were injured when their factory van crashed into a broken-down workers' bus on the Eastern Dispersal Link (EDL). Johor Baru (South) police chief Assistant Commissioner Azrul Hishan Mohd Shaffei said investigations found that the van was travelling towards Singapore when it approached the stationary factory bus, which had broken down in the right lane. The van hit the bus's rear left side.

items.title: Southern Score Builders' subsidiary secured data centre electrical works in Port Dickson
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Southern Score Builders Bhd, through its 51 per cent-owned subsidiary SJEE Engineering Sdn Bhd, has secured two subcontract agreements worth a combined RM146.8 million for electrical works at two data centre projects in Port Dickson, Negri Sembilan. Southern Score said the first project's Phase 1 substantial completion is scheduled for Oct 22, 2027, followed by Phase 2 on Jan 21, 2028. For the second project, Phase 1 substantial completion is targeted for Jan 10, 2028, while Phase 2 is scheduled for April 10, 2028.

items.title: Nadma deploys 102,000 personnel ahead of 2026/2027 northeast monsoon
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — The National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) has mobilised nearly 102,000 personnel from various departments and agencies, along with 40,000 operational assets, in preparation for the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon (MTL). Nadma Deputy Director of Operations Datuk Dr Abdul Gapar Abu Bakar said the preparations also included 8,321 temporary relief centres nationwide, with a combined capacity of up to 1.9 million flood victims. Commenting on ground-level operational coordination, Abdul Gapar said district officers are responsible for mobilising initial flood response by activating the District Disaster Operations Control Centre.

items.title: Re-ignite the Malaysian Dream, Lim Kit Siang urges Melaka voters
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Veteran DAP leader Lim Kit Siang today called on voters in Melaka to “re-ignite the Malaysian Dream”, describing Transport Minister Anthony Loke's resignation as a starting point for renewed efforts to build a united and world-class Malaysia. Lim traced the roots of the “Malaysian Dream” to before independence, citing Chinese educationist Lim Lian Geok's 1956 message to Utusan Melayu on the need to cultivate a Malaysian mindset. Nevertheless, Lim urged Malaysians not to abandon the aspirations of the Malaysian Dream.

items.title: Monash University showcases postgraduate pathways for Malaysians at Peak TRX
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Students and working professionals looking to advance their careers through postgraduate education can explore their options at Postgraduate Education Advancement & Knowledge (Peak) TRX, organised by Monash University on Nov 21, 2026. The event will be held at Kimpton Naluria, Kuala Lumpur, and aims to help prospective postgraduate students understand the study pathways available and how further education can support their personal and professional aspirations. EXPLORING NEW PATHWAYS As industries evolve and workplace demands change, postgraduate education offers opportunities to deepen expertise, broaden knowledge and develop skills aligned with career goals.

items.title: Flood situation worsens in Selangor as evacuees increase, improves in Perak
items.summary: In Selangor, the number of flood evacuees at five PPS in Kuala Selangor increased to 1,032 people, from 289 families, compared with 945 people from 265 families this morning. According to the Social Welfare Department's (JKM) InfoBencana portal, Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Dato’ Maharaja Lela housed the highest number of evacuees, at 416, followed by Sekolah Rendah Agama Bukit Kuching (287), SK Parit Mahang (238), Sekolah Agama Batu 8 Ijok (77) and SK Jaya Setia (12). In Perak, the number of flood evacuees in Hilir Perak district decreased to 330 people, from 94 families, compared with 380 people, from 108 families, this morning.

items.title: Zahid eyes BN-PN sweep in Melaka, calls for 'blue wave' [WATCH]
items.summary: AYER KEROH: Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman and Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has expressed confidence that the BN-Perikatan Nasional (PN) alliance can secure all 28 Melaka state seats, urging voters to turn their support into a "blue wave" when polls open this Saturday. God willing, we will continue to turn the state of Melaka completely blue this coming Saturday." A total of 79 candidates are contesting all 28 seats in the 16th Melaka election, comprising 11 straight fights, 11 three-cornered contests and six four-cornered battles.

items.title: Anwar, Koh pay tribute to Chet Singh, Penang industrialisation pioneer
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Penang's emergence as a world-class electrical and electronics hub was shaped in large part by former Penang Development Corporation (PDC) general manager Datuk Seri Chet Singh Karam Singh, who died yesterday aged 90. Anwar said Chet Singh's contributions had also created employment opportunities, stimulated economic growth and laid important foundations for the country's industrial development. Former Penang chief minister Tan Sri Dr Koh Tsu Koon described Chet Singh as the engineer of Penang's industrialisation.

items.title: Tragedy on the Melaka campaign trail: Car hits lorry, Alor Gajah PKR deputy chief dies in crash outside campaign operations room
items.summary: JASIN, Nov 11 — An aide of the Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate for the Asahan seat in the Melaka election was killed today when the car he was driving collided with a lorry, three days to voting day. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also PH chairman, paid tribute to J. Samivel, 62, in a Facebook post today, noting that the deceased was also Alor Gajah PKR deputy division chief. Brother Samivel, the representative of the Harapan candidate for the Asahan state seat, was killed in a road accident this afternoon.

items.title: Nvidia's clubby board faces a sticky 'honey pot' test
items.summary: REVELATIONS that Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang had an affair with a businesswoman suspected of being a Chinese spy have forced the chipmaker's board to confront more than ordinary executive misconduct, raising existential questions for the company and concerns about the board's ability to investigate its CEO independently. US President Donald Trump said on Monday the FBI is investigating Huang's relationship, a day after Nvidia's board launched an internal investigation "regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports," according to an email Huang sent to Nvidia employees and released by the company. Nvidia co-founder Huang, 63, has no obvious successor, as well as close ties to Trump.

items.title: Alphabet eyes US$3bil Hong Kong, Singapore bond sale, sources say
items.summary: One of the people added that the sales would likely raise at least US$2.2 billion, with Alphabet considering minimum sizes of HK$8 billion (US$1 billion) for the Hong Kong dollar portion and S$1.5 billion (US$1.2 billion) for the Singapore dollar portion. Alphabet last week raised EUR6 billion (US$6.7 billion) through a euro-denominated bond sale. It also sold US$25 billion of US dollar bonds in August and A$5.5 billion (US$3.8 billion) Australian dollar bonds in the same month.

items.title: Malaysia lowers December crude palm oil reference price, maintains duty at 10pct
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has lowered its December crude palm oil reference price, a change that maintains the export duty at 10 per cent, a circular on the Malaysian Palm Oil Board website showed on Wednesday. The world's second-largest palm oil exporter calculated a reference price of RM4,259.70 (US$1,046.10) per tonne for December. The export tax structure starts at 3.0 per cent for crude palm oil in a RM2,250 to RM2,400 per-tonne range.

items.title: ECRL set to drive Terengganu's economic growth, boost tourism
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU: The East Coast Rail Link (ECRL), which is scheduled to commence operations in mid-December, is expected to serve as a catalyst for economic growth in Terengganu, said Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar. He said the state government is encouraging entrepreneurs and business owners to seize the opportunities offered by the new rail network and maximise its potential. The 242-kilometre ECRL alignment in Terengganu features six stations: Chukai, Kemasik, Dungun, Kuala Terengganu, Bandar Permaisuri and Jertih.

items.title: Funding Malaysia’s SMEs is about quality and not quantity, says economy minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — The government wants to improve the quality of financing for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) to strengthen local firms’ global competitiveness and enable workers to earn higher wages and hold better-quality jobs. Although Malaysia had recorded encouraging economic growth, Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said today that structural challenges still needed to be addressed so that SMEs could expand and improve productivity. “Particularly in ensuring productivity improvements that can eventually translate into higher wages and quality employment,” he told reporters after the launch of the World Bank’s 33rd Malaysia Economic Monitor, titled ‘From Quantity to Quality: Financing Malaysia’s Productive SMEs’, here today.

items.title: Kelantan exco shake-up: Deputy MB says Bersatu rep’s appointment not renewed, with Sultan’s consent
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Nov 11 — Ayer Lanas assemblyman Datuk Kamarudin Md Nor’s appointment as a Kelantan state executive council (exco) member was not renewed, effective November 9. Kelantan Deputy Menteri Besar Datuk Dr Mohamed Fadzli Hassan said the decision had received the consent of the Sultan of Kelantan, Sultan Muhammad V. He said the two portfolios previously held by Kamarudin would be redistributed to two existing exco members to ensure the smooth running of state administration. Kamarudin previously oversaw the Tourism, Culture, Arts and Heritage portfolio.

items.title: Skudai Deepavali fireworks stunt ends in court for four, one just 16
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 11 — Four men, including a secondary school student, claimed trial at the Magistrate’s Court here today to charges of setting off fireworks on a main road during Deepavali last Sunday. The accused – P. Ruban, 20; S. Tharun, 18; H. Periuthiv, 19; and a 16-year-old – entered their pleas after the charges were read to them separately. The incident allegedly took place at 1.30am last Sunday on Jalan Skudai-Gelang Patah, near the Taman Nesa traffic lights junction in Skudai.

items.title: Anwar: ‘Hundreds of years of service’ no excuse, corrupt people belong in prison
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said that even hundreds of years of service cannot justify letting anyone plunder the wealth of the people and the country. He added that those who commit corruption belong in prison. “Even hundreds of years of service cannot be a reason for us to let anyone plunder and rob the wealth of the people and the country.

items.title: What are the terms of Najib’s house arrest? Saifuddin Nasution to explain in Dewan Rakyat
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said he will address the Dewan Rakyat tomorrow to lay out the operational conditions and custodial restrictions governing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s transition into house arrest. The upcoming parliamentary briefing follows Najib’s arrival at his Jalan Langgak Duta residence in Kuala Lumpur at 9.27pm yesterday to begin serving the remainder of his six-year SRC International sentence at home. His release from prison walls was finalised after High Court Judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin set aside a contentious November 6 discharge order and replaced it in full, explicitly authorizing Najib to serve his custodial sentence at his private home until August 23, 2028.

items.title: Monsoon surge triggers continuous rain alert for Kelantan, Terengganu and Sabah until tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 – The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MET Malaysia) has issued an updated continuous rain alert for parts of Kelantan, Terengganu, and Sabah, as an incoming monsoon surge threatens to trigger persistent downpours through tomorrow. In an advisory released at 2.00pm today, the department explained that atmospheric simulation models indicate a monsoon surge is entering regional airspace, creating unstable weather conditions likely to dump sustained, heavy precipitation along the eastern seaboard of Peninsular Malaysia and eastern Sabah over the next 24 hours. In neighbouring Terengganu, the warning encompasses the northern and coastal districts of Besut, Setiu, Kuala Terengganu, and Kuala Nerus.

items.title: Loke: JPJ’s war on overloaded lorries must continue even without me, as it involves human lives
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 11 — In his parting words to the Transport Ministry, Anthony Loke today urged the Road Transport Department to continue its “war” against overloading in commercial vehicles even after he leaves as transport minister. Loke, who effectively resigned as transport minister yesterday, said there would be people cheering that the minister who refused to compromise on overloading, and who they felt interfered with their livelihood, was gone. “‘The minister has left, we can overload again like in the past, no problem,’” he said in his 48-minute speech at the Transport Ministry here, describing how overloaders would feel.

items.title: Umno says opposing Najib’s house arrest could amount to challenging King’s constitutional powers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Umno has warned that actions perceived as protests against the conditional pardon granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, including the house arrest provision, could be construed as challenging the Yang di-Pertuan Agong’s constitutional authority. In a media statement posted on his Facebook page, Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the party believed the conditional pardon granted under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution reflected the King’s constitutional powers and rights, which must be respected by all institutions and the public. The party said any action taken in protest, including using the conditional pardon decree as justification, could be seen as an act of defiance against the King’s constitutional authority.

items.title: Rosmah not allowed to live with Najib during house arrest, Umno leader says
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s family members and other individuals are not permitted to live with him while he serves the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest, according to Umno Women’s executive council member Datuk Nurulhidayah Ahmad Zahid. Nurulhidayah said Najib’s wife, Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor, is expected to stay at her residence in Pavilion instead of the Taman Duta house where he is serving his sentence, Harian Metro reported today. Responding to questions on Threads about the implementation of the house arrest order, Nurulhidayah said the Jalan Langgak Duta residence had been gazetted as a prison, meaning standard prison rules would apply.

items.title: ‘Camera must follow the schedule’: Hannah Yeoh says as DBKL makes body cams compulsory for field operations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) will equip its enforcement unit with 200 additional body-worn cameras, bringing its total number of devices to 305. Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh and Kuala Lumpur mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud announced the expansion at DBKL’s 57th Enforcement Day parade in Bandar Tun Razak today. Fadlun said the additional cameras were part of DBKL’s efforts to modernise enforcement operations, with footage providing a record of officers’ actions in the event of complaints or disputes.

items.title: BN MPs want AG to take leave over four-day delay in Najib’s house arrest
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Several Barisan Nasional (BN) MPs today called for the Attorney General (AG) to be placed on temporary leave pending an independent investigation into the delay in implementing Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest. Manndzri said Najib’s continued detention at Kajang Prison for four more days could amount to unlawful detention, particularly as no court order had been obtained to justify the delay. Najib was transferred from Kajang Prison to his residence last night to serve the remainder of his six-year SRC International prison sentence under house arrest, following a fresh High Court order.

items.title: MCMC finds 23 internet quality breaches in Muar, takes action against telcos
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has issued eight non-compliance notices to telecommunications companies after an audit this year uncovered 23 breaches of internet service quality standards at 16 locations in the Muar parliamentary constituency. Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said the audit, conducted on six service providers between Jan 1 and Oct 1, found that only 18 of the 34 locations assessed in Muar met the Mandatory Standards for Quality of Service (MSQoS). Syed Saddiq had wanted to know the measures to address poor internet service quality and limited connectivity in parts of Muar, despite data from the National Digital Network Plan (JENDELA) showing 100 per cent coverage in Parit Amat, Sungai Kelat, Tanjung Tohor and Sungai Muda.

items.title: DAP yet to pick candidate to replace Loke as transport minister, for PM to decide
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 11 — Anthony Loke today confirmed that DAP has yet to discuss a candidate to replace him as transport minister, a post he resigned from with immediate effect yesterday. Asked by reporters at the Transport Ministry here whether DAP had discussed a potential successor, Loke gave a brief “not yet” response. “This is the prime minister's jurisdiction, discuss with him,” he replied when asked whether or not the decision would be left to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.

items.title: Ex-Tabung Haji chief Azeez gets court nod to challenge IRB’s cancellation of RM4.8m tax deal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Former Lembaga Tabung Haji chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim today secured High Court permission to challenge the Inland Revenue Board’s (IRB) decision to revoke a RM4.8 million tax settlement he says he had fully paid. The court today allowed his application for leave to commence judicial review, paving the way for a full hearing on whether IRB was legally entitled to cancel the agreement. The dispute centres on a settlement agreement signed on February 9, 2022, covering Azeez’s tax and penalties for the assessment years 2011 to 2020.

items.title: Trader suspected of sourcing frozen chicken from Thailand arrested in raid
items.summary: -KOTA BHARU, Nov 11 — A frozen chicken trader in Pasir Tumboh, here, is suspected of obtaining between 300 and 500 boxes of stock from a supplier in Thailand before selling them at his wholesale premises. General Operations Force (GOF) Southeast Brigade Commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the matter came to light following the arrest of a 38-year-old man during an Op Salju Mega raid at a premises along Jalan Pasir Puteh, Kampung Pasir Tumboh, at about noon yesterday. “An inspection by the enforcement team uncovered 209 boxes of frozen chicken, weighing 2,508 kilogrammes and worth RM42,845, stored in a refrigerated container at the premises,” he said in a statement last night.

items.title: Social media firms face Dec 28 deadline under Online Safety Act
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Licensed social media service providers must submit their Online Safety Plans to the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) by Dec 28 at the latest, in compliance with the Online Safety Act 2025 (Act 866). She said social media platforms were also expected to implement user age verification requirements in early January 2027, following the end of the current transition period. Teo said MCMC had issued directives to social media service providers, including Meta, TikTok and Google, to ensure the implementation of age verification mechanisms.

items.title: ‘A leader must be decisive’: Loke says ‘conscience is clear’ as he reflects on time as minister
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 11 — Anthony Loke today said his conscience is clear as he had done his best during his nearly four years as transport minister, while reaffirming that his resignation took effect yesterday following the court order allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve his sentence under house arrest. Speaking at the Transport Ministry’s monthly assembly and Deepavali celebrations today, Loke thanked everyone in the ministry and apologised to anyone who may have been affected by his words, actions or past mistakes. Loke said civil servants were “most worried and disliked it the most when a minister sits on a decision, sits on files, not making decisions”.

items.title: SAR operation resumes for three missing in Kuala Kubu Baharu water surge
items.summary: HULU SELANGOR, Nov 11 — The search resumed today for three foreign men still missing after being swept away by a water surge at Sungai Luit, near the Sungai Pertak picnic site in Kampung Orang Asli Pertak, Kuala Kubu Baharu here. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the search was focused on two locations, namely Pertak Bridge and the Sungai Selangor Dam. Ashrul Riezal said the three missing men were identified as a Yemeni national and two Indian nationals.

items.title: LPT3’s winning bidder will foot the bill, Works Ministry expects the cost to top RM10b
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — The government has not proposed a hybrid financing model for the East Coast Expressway Phase 3 (LPT3), even though it adopted one for a highway project in Penang, Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan said today. “Hybrid financing is something new. Ahmad said the government had to weigh its existing investments in major east coast transport infrastructure before deciding on a financing arrangement.

items.title: Sixteen, including six children, rescued in Sungai Bakap flash floods
items.summary: NIBONG TEBAL, Nov 11 — Sixteen people, including six children, from three families were rescued after their homes were inundated by flash floods in Kampung Sethu, Sungai Bakap, here early this morning. Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations John Sagun Francis said continuous heavy rain caused several houses in the area to be flooded about three feet, trapping residents in their homes. He said the department received an emergency call at 12.40 am and dispatched six firefighters from the Sungai Bakap Fire and Rescue Station to the scene to carry out the rescue operation.

items.title: More than 1,300 displaced as floods worsen in Perak, Selangor
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — A total of 1,325 people from 373 families remained at flood relief centres in Perak and Selangor this morning. In Perak, the number of flood evacuees rose to 380 from 108 families this morning, up from 348 from 99 families yesterday afternoon, with all of them housed at two relief centres. Meanwhile, in Selangor, the number of flood evacuees at five relief centres in Kuala Selangor also increased to 945 from 265 families, compared with 848 from 236 families yesterday.
